name: 46,XX Disorder of Gonadal Development

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Criteria for Disorders of Sex Development

criteria.description: Presence of 46,XX karyotype confirmed by chromosomal analysis
Histological evidence of dysgenetic or ovotesticular gonadal tissue
Clinical presentation of ambiguous or atypical external genitalia
Abnormal sex steroid hormone levels inconsistent with typical female development
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in sex determination (e.g., SRY translocation, SOX9, RSPO1)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of 46,XX karyotype with gonadal dysgenesis or ovotesticular tissue plus ambiguous genitalia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including cytogenetics, histopathology, and endocrinology.

pathognomonic.notes: Variable degrees of genital ambiguity including clitoromegaly or labioscrotal fusion

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of ovotestis or dysgenetic gonadal tissue

common.notes: Delayed or absent menarche in adolescence

searchTerms: high LH and FSH hormone levels

common.notes: Detected on imaging or surgical exploration

occasional.notes: Enlarged clitoris due to androgen exposure
Incomplete development of secondary sexual characteristics

rare.notes: Malignant transformation risk in dysgenetic gonads

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric manifestations related to gender dysphoria
searchTerms: mental health issues from gender dysphoria
psychiatric symptoms related to gender identity
psychological distress due to gender incongruence

laboratory: Abnormal sex steroid hormone profile (low estradiol, variable androgens)
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing streak gonads or ovotesticular tissue
Absence or hypoplasia of uterus or other Müllerian structures
genetic: Absence of SRY gene or presence of SRY translocation
Mutations in sex-determining genes such as SOX9, RSPO1, FOXL2
other: Histopathological confirmation of gonadal tissue type
Risk of gonadoblastoma necessitating gonadectomy in some cases

distinguishingFeatures: Female external genitalia with absent or rudimentary Müllerian structures
Normal or elevated androgen levels with androgen receptor defects
Signs of salt-wasting or virilization due to adrenal androgen excess

redFlags: Ambiguous genitalia at birth requiring urgent evaluation
Rapid virilization during infancy or childhood
Presence of gonadal tumors or suspicious gonadal masses
references: Hughes IA, et al. Consensus statement on management of intersex disorders. Arch Dis Child. 2006.
Orphanet: 46,XX disorder of gonadal development. Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases. 2021.
Lee PA, et al. Disorders of sex development. Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2016.
